Welcome to the tutorial on building your own RCompendium.

# I - Initial setup

## 1 - Positron 

First, if it is your first time using Positron, you will need to foloww a few steps to setup your environment. 
You can follow these instrutions to set up your environment: https://frbcesab.github.io/rsetup/chapters/reproducible-research.html

## 2 - RStudio

TBD

If you have already set up your environment, you can skip to the next section.

# II - Create a new RCompendium

Create a new Positron project: New Folder from Template > R Project

- Choose a name for your project (without punctuation), e.g., practice
- Select the location where the new project will be created
- Do not initialize git
- Click Next
- Verify that the latest version is selected
- Do not initialize renv
- Click Create

First, create a .R file called "setup.R". This file will be used to write the command to create the RCompendium.

Second, run these commands in the "setup.R" file to create the RCompendium:

```R
file.create(".here") #locate all future files

utils::file.edit(here::here("README.md")) #README file

rcompendium::add_description() #Description file
rcompendium::add_license(license = "GPL-2") #Add a license
rcompendium::add_compendium(compendium = c("data", "analyses", "R", "figures", "outputs"))
utils::file.edit(here::here("make.R")) #Add a make.R
```

# III - Load your project

To use your now setup RCompendium, you need to setup your make.r file. This file will be used to load all the packages and functions you will need for your project.

Packages called as library() or require() will be added to the Depends field of the DESCRIPTION file
Packages called as :: or ::: will be added to the Imports field of the DESCRIPTION file

If you need to list some packages in the Imports field, you can add library(package you want to call) in the setup.R file

```r
#Execute the scripts and looks for all packages used in the project and add them to the DESCRIPTION file

rdeps::add_deps()

# Install packages listed in the DESCRIPTION file 
devtools::install_deps(upgrade="never")

# Load project (packages and functions)
devtools::load_all()
```
